Most recent work

Six sites finished since the last report, each one blocked on something different, each one unblocked a different way

Dr. Leanne Katz-Levin, PhD is a clinical psychologist and medical educator at New York Medical College, where she is Director of Patient Care for the School of Medicine and an Assistant Professor in the Department of Medicine. She has specialised in chronic illness management since 1995: chronic pain, cardiac, pulmonary and neurological conditions, and the caregivers who are so often left out of the conversation. She runs a research laboratory on chronic illness and Long COVID, teaches neuropsychology and psychological assessment, sat on the New York Mayor’s Commission to Combat Domestic Violence, and wrote the caregiver chapter in a published book on autism.

Her file had been blocked for six weeks and the reason was not laziness. Every chat before this one searched Marquis Who’s Who and its newswires, correctly finding nothing, because she was never a Marquis client. Her placement is with a different publisher entirely. The sheet also spells her name three ways against her own published profile. Both were settled before a word was written.

  • The name was wrong on the sheet, and it was not corrected quietlyRow 36 reads Leanne Levine. Her own published profile reads Dr. Leanne Katz-Levin, and her employer’s staff directory reads Leanne J Levin. Her email address on the sheet is what ties the three together. The site uses the spelling she publishes under. The sheet is Alexander’s and is never edited silently, so the difference is raised rather than fixed.
  • Her one award was left off the page on purposeThe only entry under honours on her profile is a paid membership of the same kind as a Who’s Who listing. Paid placements are never shown on a client site as an honour, so rather than dress it up the site carries no awards section at all.
  • Checked against her employer, not just her own profileHer job title, her department and her research were verified against New York Medical College’s own directory and a peer reviewed paper she co-authored in 2025. Where the sources disagree on her exact title, the page uses her own wording and the disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed over.
  • Her field is trauma, and the pictures do not trade on itShe works with dementia, caregiving, child and elder abuse and domestic violence. None of that is depicted. The twelve pictures show the professional work only: listening, teaching, thinking. Everyone in frame sits at the same eye level. She is a psychologist, not a physician, so she is never put in a white coat.

Jonathan Shane Wallingford is president of JSB Industrial Solutions in Tollesboro, Kentucky, the company behind the Economy Ball Mill line: the large rotating mills that grind material for mining, mineral processing, recycling and rare earth mineral recovery. He took the company through the COVID period after a heavy loss of contracts, rebuilt its route to market, finished a new manufacturing plant in early 2026 and turned the old building into a full scale laboratory. He sells equipment into Australia, Belgium, Romania, Mexico and Canada.

  • His two releases contradict each other, so no year is publishedOne says he has been president since 2012, the other since 2013. One dates his degrees 2013 and 2014, the other 2011 and 2013. One dates an award 2016, the other 2025. Rather than pick a side, the page says he has led the company for more than a decade and names his degrees without years. Both versions are kept on file.
  • The Wall Street Journal placement is not presented as an honourIt belongs to the same paid programme as the listing itself, so it is treated the same way: recorded, not displayed.
  • The reference photograph came from the release itselfNo portrait of him existed on his company site. The attachment on his second release turned out to carry a clear headshot, which is his own published photograph and clears the sourcing rule without asking him for anything.
  • The reserved template was dropped because it did not fitA marketing agency layout had been set aside for him: split colour banner, pricing tables, a team of three, a blog and testimonials. None of it survives contact with an industrial manufacturer, so it was released for another client and the site was built on a construction demo instead.

Lawrence Steven Cosentino is a risk control consultant at Travelers working in equipment breakdown: boilers, electrical plant and rotating machinery, surveyed and quantified before they fail. Eight years as a nuclear electrician in the United States Navy, much of it submerged aboard the USS Jacksonville and the USS Missouri, then a loss control specialist at Hartford Steam Boiler, where he was recognised in 2019 for exemplary integrity. He holds Lean Six Sigma Green and Black Belts from Villanova and is reading for an MBA in business analytics.

  • The first site in the portfolio built without a single photograph of the clientNo photograph of him is published anywhere, and the usual sources were all checked: both of his releases, his employer, his guild and veterans organisations, and the church where he serves as a deacon. His name is on the church roll with no picture beside it. Rather than invent a face for a real man, the site was built so that it does not need one. Every picture is plant, machinery or place, and the day he sends a portrait it goes straight in.
  • The form was rebuilt before it shippedThe demo’s own enquiry form posts to a PHP mailer that cannot run on this hosting. It would have looked perfect and delivered nothing. It now posts to his address on the sheet, spelled exactly as the sheet spells it.

William C. Rense, PhD taught geography and earth science at Shippensburg University of Pennsylvania from 1980 until he retired in 2004, after several years teaching at the University of Louisianna at Lafayette. His field is physical geography, and inside it hydrology and climatology. He took his doctorate at Oregon State University, chaired the promotion committee on his campus for three years, wrote the entry on Pennsylvania for the World Book Encyclopedia, and from Colorado still files a monthly article on the weather to the Allenspark Wind.

  • One source, so the page says only what that source saysHis release is the only published account of his career anywhere. The Pennsylvania Geographical Society’s own list of past award winners corroborates the 2007 Distinguished Service Award and names the department his release leaves out. Nothing beyond those two sources is on the page. Where the record gives no year for a degree, the page prints no year.
  • The 1994 award is published without an awarding bodyThe record gives the award and the year and does not say who conferred it. The Pennsylvania Geographical Society runs awards of that name, which makes it a plausible giver, but plausible is not confirmed, so the page names nobody rather than guess. It says so on the page, in as many words.
  • The reference photograph came off the Times Square screenNo portrait of him is published anywhere. The attachment on his release is a photograph of the Marquis screen in Times Square carrying his placement, with his headshot on the screen. That panel was cropped out, upscaled nine times and colour balanced before use, and the image model was told the source was a display, so it would render daylight skin tone instead of copying the screen’s colour cast.
  • No contact form, and no address invented to fill the gapHe is not on the customer sheet, so no address for him is held on file. Rather than point a form at a guess or lift an address out of a directory of residential records, the page carries no form at all and says why in its own footer.
  • Both names for the Louisiana institution are keptHis release spells it University of Louisianna at Lafayette where he taught, and University of Southwestern Louisiana where he took his degrees. They are the same institution under its old and new names. The page uses each name where the source uses it, rather than merging them or correcting the spelling quietly.

Cindy A. Okolo, DNP, APRN, FNP-BC is a family nurse practitioner and primary care provider in Poplar Bluff, Missouri, with more than seventeen years in healthcare. She took her Doctor of Nursing Practice at Midwestern University in 2025 and her Master of Science in Nursing on the family nurse practitioner track at Governors State University. Before primary care she worked high acuity and hospitalist settings across Elkhart General, Goshen General, Ottumwa Regional and University of Chicago Medicine, in critical care, internal medicine, family medicine and dermatology, and she has taught nursing online. She is certified in Advanced Cardiac Life Support and Basic Life Support, belongs to six professional bodies, and speaks English and Igbo.

  • Blocked for six weeks because the search was aimed at the wrong publisherHer file sat open since 14 September with no source. Every chat before this one searched Marquis Who’s Who and its newswires and correctly found nothing, because she was never a Marquis client. Her placement is with Americas Best In Medicine, the same publisher as Dr. Katz-Levin. Tahir supplied the link himself and the site was built the same day. The claim file now records the publisher so no chat re-opens the Marquis search for her.
  • Four paid recognitions, and not one of them appears on her pageThe Americas Best In Medicine profile, two newswire releases carrying the same placement and a Pinnacle Professional of the Year line are all paid placements of the same kind as the listing itself. They are sources for the facts and nothing more, so the site carries no awards section at all. Her licence numbers are left off as well.
  • Two template sections were deleted rather than filled with invented copyThe demo ships with testimonials and a blog. No patient testimonial of hers is published anywhere, and inventing one for a clinician is not a small liberty, so both sections were removed instead. The three figures on the page are the only numbers her sources actually give: seventeen years in healthcare, four hospital systems, six professional bodies. Nothing about patient numbers, outcomes or ratings is published, so none is shown.
  • The enquiry form was rebuilt before it shippedThe demo’s own form posts to a PHP mailer that cannot run on this hosting: it would have looked perfect and delivered nothing. It now posts to her address on the sheet, spelled exactly as the sheet spells it. She clicks one activation email the first time it is used.

Marvin J. Schwarz, MD, JD is a child and adolescent psychiatrist in Skokie, Illinois, and the founder of Associates in Adolescent Psychiatry, the practice he started in 1961 and still presides over. He took his medical degree at Wayne State in 1950 and his law degree at Loyola in 1983, and has used the two together ever since, advising government agencies and health care providers on how federal rules, state rules and daily operations fit together when care is delivered and when it is paid for. Before the practice there was a postdoctoral year at MIT, graduate study at Ohio State, technology work at Oak Ridge, and a United States Air Force posting running a pulmonary physiology laboratory and acting as medical liaison to the aircraft nuclear propulsion programme. He directed child psychiatry at Rush and at Michael Reese, and has taught at the University of Illinois, Indiana University and the Stritch School of Medicine at Loyola.

  • He was written off as unbuildable, and the source was on our own mastheadHis file had been marked as having no published source anywhere. The Dynamo Times sitemap had never been read by any chat, and his profile was sitting on it. Reading that one file unblocked him and four other clients in an afternoon. The sitemap is now a standing first check, before any Marquis search.
  • Two paid recognitions were deliberately left off the pageA Marquis Lifetime Achievement Award and an American Health Council designation both appear in his material. Both are paid placements of the same kind as the listing itself, so they are sources for the facts and nothing more. The page carries no awards section at all.
  • The portrait on his own press release was not a photographThe image file on the release is a placeholder card with his initials on it, and the filename gives no sign of that. The real reference is the headshot attached to his newswire release. The twelve pictures on the site were built from that and checked against it on a contact sheet before anything was wired in, with his age, which is about ninety nine, the thing most likely to go wrong and the thing checked hardest. The page states in plain words that the pictures are AI generated illustrations made with his approval.
  • The template did not fit, so the page was written without oneOnly four unused demos were left and none suited a psychiatrist who is also an attorney and a laboratory scientist. The page was written from nothing on the reserved slot, in a paper and ink palette, with no vendor framework at all. That dropped seventeen megabytes of unused library code: the finished site is twenty three files and 1.2 megabytes. Ninety seven contrast measurements at four widths, zero failures, tightest 5.10 to 1.

All six were built the same way and held to the same checks: nothing on a page that is not in the client’s own published material, every file verified one by one against the published copy, and a full contrast audit with zero failures before anything went live.
